newsitem.title: USA: US not rushed to reach WTO pact with China-Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: US not rushed to reach WTO pact with China-Barshefsky.

text.p: The United States will not rush to conclude an agreement with China on the terms of its entry into the World Trade Organisation, U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Wednesday.

Commenting on reports that negotiations have stalled, Barshefsky said, "There's no race here." She said the only important issue was that "whatever is agreed to is going to have to be very, very good."

Barshefsky told reporters that some progress has been made in the negotiations. For example, China had pledged not to subsidise agricultural exports, which is very important because of its huge productive capacity, she said.
China does not currently subsidise farm exports. But "there was a growing concern" that China could use export subsidies in future years to break into foreign markets, she said.
The United States also expects China to forward new offers on tariffs and services sometime in late August or early September, Barshefsky said.

"I don't think we can prejudge one way or another," Barshefsky responded when asked whether those offers could lead to an agreement by the time President Bill Clinton meets with Chinese President Jiang Zemin in Washington in October.
